page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-48-lssd is an x86_64 instance from the Network Optimized family designed for memory-intensive and data-heavy enterprise workloads. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs paired with 372 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory allocation of approximately 7.75 GB per core. The instance includes 3,221 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage distributed across eight drives, without discrete hardware accelerators.

From an architectural perspective, the tight integration of 48 dedicated compute cores and high-density local NVMe storage reduces external block storage overhead and provides low-latency disk access. The provision of 372 GB RAM supports large in-memory working sets. While benchmark metrics are unavailable for this specific configuration, the combination of dedicated compute, high memory density, and local flash arrays delivers a balanced profile for transactional processing.

From an operational perspective, the bundled 3,221 GB NVMe tier offers cost efficiency by removing the requirement to attach external high-IOPS persistent storage volumes for high-throughput scratch or working data. However, local SSD storage is ephemeral, requiring external replication or snapshot mechanisms for persistent data protection. Network architecture accommodates high data flow, though public IPv4 routing requires external provisioning as zero complimentary addresses are supplied.

Target workloads for this configuration include in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, big data analytics engines, intermediate extract-transform-load (ETL) processing stages, and distributed relational databases requiring immediate, high-throughput local disk storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-48-lssd is a network-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-centric and IOPS-heavy computing requirements. Powered by an x86_64 architecture, the instance supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 372 GB of system RAM, providing an allocation of 7.75 GB per core. Storage is provisioned locally through 3,221 GB of fast NVMe SSD media configured across eight bundled drives, eliminating dependency on external block volumes for primary scratch data. The server does not feature GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By consolidating dense memory and dedicated processing with high-speed local flash storage, the configuration achieves strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for input-output intensive tasks. It is well-matched for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput data pipelines, ETL stages, and high-performance transactional database engines requiring rapid local data access.
